gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a named tester measured on the Vantrue N4S with all three cameras recording: EricSan on DashCamTalk logged 2592×1944 front plus 1440p cabin and rear, each at 30 fps, at 16.0 / 14.3 / 14.3 Mb/s (about 20 GB an hour), drawing about 7.1 W driving and about 4.3 W in low-bitrate parking mode.
standout_why: I compared against the three rival pages I could open. productbible.com (cited) names the N4S at $199.99 but reports maker specs only, with no measurement. dattatecblog.com (cited) gives only its author's install time and '64GB holds roughly 6 hours' for the Redtiger F17 3CH. us.my-best.com (cited) does have its own measurements (horizontal field of view and plate-legibility scores), but for the VIOFO T130, the older Vantrue N4 and six others; it covers neither the N4S, the Redtiger F17 nor the Rexing C3, and it has no bitrate, frame-rate or power figures. So rivals hold part of this angle (mybest), but none has per-channel bitrate, frame rate or power draw for any under-$200 pick. vortexradar.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and caranddriver.com could not be fetched, so neither was compared; the other uncited results were not opened.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue N4S as the pick at the budget line, and it is the only under-$200 3-channel candidate for which I found a named tester's figures with all three channels recording. Those figures show 30 fps on every channel, about 20 GB an hour (roughly 12.7 hours on a 256 GB card) and about 4.3 W in low-bitrate parking mode (the tester estimated a bit over 60 hours on a 276 Wh pack). The caveat is bitrate: its 16.0 Mb/s front stream compares with 45.9 Mb/s that the same tester logged on a VIOFO A139 Pro front camera. It also weakens ChatGPT's Redtiger F17 pick: every named measurement I found is for the F17 Elite, which is $227.98 and up at Redtiger's store and so over budget, and testers logged it at 25 fps front and 20 to 25 fps on the 1080p channel. The plain F17 ($129.99 at Redtiger) and the Rexing C3 have no named measurement that I found. For our own rows (the Botslab G980H 4-camera, and the DDPAI Z60T if added) I found no named measurement of bitrate or power, so they cannot be ranked on this angle. I could not open vantrue.com myself (HTTP 429 three times), so the N4S's $199.99 is the figure from your 2026-11-21 partner table; it is one cent under the budget and wants a re-read before publishing.

findings.label: Resolution, frame rate and bitrate with front + cabin + rear recording together (DashCamTalk reviewer EricSan, post #1, 2025-06-11)
findings.value: Front 2592×1944 at 30 fps, 16.0 Mb/s; cabin 1440p at 30 fps, 14.3 Mb/s; rear 1440p at 30 fps, 14.3 Mb/s
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Read from the recorded files. Post #1 gives the cabin and rear width as 2592×1440; post #16 (2025-06-12) gives the rear as 2560×1440. With front + cabin only, both record 2592×1944 at 30 fps, 16.0 Mb/s each. Arithmetic: 16.0 + 14.3 + 14.3 = 44.6 Mb/s = about 20.1 GB per hour, so about 6.4 h on a 128 GB card and about 12.7 h on 256 GB (decimal GB) before looping.

findings.label: File size per 3-minute clip, drive mode (EricSan, post #16, 2025-06-12)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Same post logs a VIOFO A139 Pro front camera at 3840×1600, 30 fps, 45.9 Mb/s (1,019,730 kB per 3 min) and its rear at 1920×1080, 16.4 Mb/s. The N4S front stream is about a third of the A139 Pro's bitrate.

findings.label: Parking mode recording, low-bitrate setting (EricSan, post #16, 2025-06-12)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: All three cameras were set to low bitrate. The reviewer also notes the supercapacitors keep the camera running 3 to 4 seconds after power is removed.

findings.label: Power draw on the hardwire kit, measured at 15.76 V (EricSan, post #25, 2025-06-15)
findings.value: Front + cabin + rear, driving: 452 mA typical (about 7.1 W). Front + cabin: 472 mA (about 7.4 W). Front only: 432 mA (about 6.8 W). Parking mode, front + rear, low-bitrate 1080p: 275 mA typical (about 4.3 W), range 158 to 393 mA.
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam, page 2 (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Digital multimeter in series with the hardwire kit's negative lead, min/max over about 20 s, typical = average of the two; the reviewer calls it 'not a super precise measurement'. The table is an image, so the figures are from the page text. The reviewer estimates 'a bit more than 60hrs' of low-bitrate parking recording from a 276 Wh LTO pack (276 / 4.3 = about 64 h). The parking figure is front + rear, not all three channels.

findings.label: Low-voltage cutoff behaviour on the hardwire kit (EricSan, post #26, 2025-06-15)
findings.value: 12.0 V setting: stays on at 12.0 V, shuts off within about a minute at 11.95 V. 11.6 V setting: stays on at 11.6 V, off at 11.55 V.
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the new Vantrue N4S Dashcam, page 2 (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: In post #34 (2025-06-17) the same reviewer lost about 6 minutes of footage on the first parking-to-drive switch, later blamed on a pre-production unit and gone after reformatting the card. jsmith (post #40) saw about a 6-second gap per parking-to-drive switch.

findings.label: Horizontal field of view measured by mybest against the maker's figure, and mybest scores
findings.value: Measured front 100° (maker 140°), rear 120° (165°), interior 110° (165°). Overall 4.49 of 5 (ranked 1 of 8), low light 5.00, high light 4.78, interior 4.00.
findings.note: A cited rival already holds this. Method: protractor and chalk line with cones every 10° from 40° to 130°; plate photographed at 12, 16 and 32 ft indoors and at 6.5 ft in about 0.1 lux, judged by ten testers. The page carries no date. mybest lists it at $181.00 on Amazon; I did not open Amazon.
